reviewer_statement: Author-side source scientific review against frozen Python 1.2. Prior direct-source oracle cases for evaluate_sparse_fpca_recovery are retained. Fifteen additional proposed full assessment-frame and provenance comparisons test all three FPCA recovery families across five scientific parameter/diagnostic domains. Shared sparse Boolean score condition and covariance correction coercion now matches published pandas/float(bool) source behavior. Direct CI and independent scientific certification are pending.
native_language_semantic_policy: Python frozen FPCA/SparseFPCA/SparseMFPCA and truth dataclasses map to explicitly typed/validated native scientific R result records; the returned assessment tuple and provenance become source-ordered registered R scientific metric lists. Core mathematical source estimands, 0-based component indexing and statistical tolerances are reviewed while runtime identity and exception classes remain language-specific.

case_evidence.description: Frozen published eyetrajectoriespy==1.2.0 recovery.py::evaluate_sparse_fpca_recovery taking typed fit and FunctionalSimulationTruth; native scientific records mapped without importing Python.

Five related typed full-source records: baseline numeric score-condition diagnostic, pandas Boolean diagnostic with float(True) PSD correction, status-only diagnostics, empty score diagnostics, and zero declared measurement-noise. Prior multi-component and tied-eigenspace source oracles retained.

Fifteen complete Python 1.2 and native R data.frame source comparisons covering three linked evaluator exports over five scientific records: all nine semantic metric columns, exact row order and missingness, absolute/relative metrics, provenance, alignment, covariance blocks, and numerical angular precision qualification.

Native source scientific records reject invalid fitted truth grid, scaling/geometry, absent sparse dimensions, invalid covariance operator shape and wrong declared quadrature; Python dataclass class identity, NumPy warning identity and arbitrary malformed runtime objects are not claimed.

Python FunctionalRecoveryAssessment metric tuple and provenance map correspond to native R scientific value records, reconstructible into exact nine-column assessment data.frame; source component numbers and alignment provenance maintained.

Univariate sparse PACE known-truth recovery with estimated covariance rather than mode-only covariance, diagnostics with pandas Boolean and numeric conversions, zero true measurement-noise boundary, PSD repair, score failures and optional noise metric.

independent_review_status: Developer-reviewed source-semantic evidence; native Linux/macOS/Windows and frozen Python 1.2 exact-head CI not yet passed, independent certification=0.
language_specific_limits: Pandas and frozen scientific dataclass runtime identities differ from native R list/assessment objects
Acos at a cosine numerically near 1 requires machine-roundoff-derived absolute angular tolerance while all other metrics use tight numerical tolerances
Python exception and NumPy warning class equality are not claimed for malformed source object identities or arbitrary custom inputs
These contracts assess known truth from supplied fits and do not certify the FPCA or sparse PACE estimation algorithms or source simulator RNG
